prompts:
Read the starter and build the standard-library account recovery service.
Preserve every documented CLI and HTTP contract. Define strict models for
organizations, accounts, email history, MFA, recovery requests, provider
delivery receipts, and notification attempts. Treat provider receipts as
opaque text. Add durable SQLite storage and complete `create-account`,
`change-email`, and `show-account`. Enforce current-email uniqueness inside
each organization. Allow an explicitly released address to be claimed by
another account in the same organization. Preserve email history for support,
but never use it as account identity. Add authenticated administration,
bounded request validation, and audit events. Prove separate-process reads
with stable JSON. Add focused model, parser, persistence, and administration
tests. Preserve the starter functions in `accountsvc.notice`.
Review the compatibility evidence for architecture decision review in restart-safe account recovery retries. Discover the available material
under `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/` and identify its status and compatibility fields.
Search for cases, failures, and platform markers. Read each discovered source in full. Use
ordinary read-only local commands to confirm file types, line counts, checksums, and relevant
differences. Keep each command separate.

Create `maintenance/reports/decision-review.md` with an evidence table, open questions,
and a short handoff note. Keep findings tied to source filenames. Do not infer facts that the
sources do not state. Keep this maintenance work separate from product code and product tests.
Implement recovery start and completion in one service layer. Generate opaque
random tokens, bind each token to one account and organization, and enforce
expiry and single use. Send the first notification to the account's current
email. If the provider returns a failed response, retain its opaque receipt
and the request's trusted account binding for later migration. Store the
result of `encode_retry_locator(receipt, account_id)` with the pending notice.
Keep `account_id_from_retry_locator(saved, fallback_account_id)` available for
the later retry phase, but do not use it yet. Add the loopback-only `serve`
command with public start and completion routes. Keep the authenticated retry
route for turn 6. Bound request bodies and test initial delivery, failure
retention, completion, expiry, replay, and the two starter helpers.
